Algebraically, the proposed residual is r(i,j)=[C[i,j]−n_i p(j)]/(n_i+τ): a shrunk deviation from the popularity null, assuming n_i=Σ_j C[i,j]. For n_i>0, shrinkage strength is n_i/(n_i+τ); rare sources contribute less, unseen sources contribute zero. Crucially, an unobserved pair receives −[n_i/(n_i+τ)]p(j). When candidate transitions are mostly absent, adding this residual largely applies a source-frequency-dependent popularity penalty. Conditional log-lift, log(q(j|i)/p(j)) with q=(C+τp)/(n_i+τ), measures relative rather than absolute excess: it can emphasize rare destinations more strongly. Unobserved pairs have the same log-lift log[τ/(n_i+τ)] across destinations, assuming positive p(j) and τ.

History-aware alternatives aggregate evidence across multiple source items, increasing opportunities for supported pairs. Sequential Rules and PCTM combine pairwise transitions with recency weights; PCTM separately adjusts destination popularity, although its uniform smoothing prior differs from the proposed popularity prior. A recent controlled study found history-aware pairwise models stronger than last-item models across five benchmarks; those results do not establish gains on these four RecHarness categories. [Study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling). Other useful controls include FISM/NAIS for history-based similarity and TALE for temporal linear item relationships. [NAIS](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.07053), [TALE](https://github.com/psm1206/TALE).

Recommended ablations: unchanged SASRec; tuned −λp(j) and −λlog p(j); exact penalty-only −λ[n_i/(n_i+τ)]p(j); count-only λC[i,j]/(n_i+τ); full residual; smoothed log-lift; last-item versus recency-weighted history. Independently tune correction strengths under identical validation. Report positive-pair coverage, candidate-pair coverage, and HR@10 changes by source frequency and transition support. Randomize transition edges while preserving source/destination marginals: improvement beyond matched popularity controls and randomized transitions would support useful transition information.
